Resolves #18980

The native WebSocket close callback supplies one `CloseEvent`; the connection read `reason` and `wasClean` from nonexistent extra arguments, so its observable event lost those fields and every clean shutdown retried. It now reads the event fields and leaves a normal clean code-1000 close closed by default. `reconnectOnCleanClose` makes the retry policy explicit: the default Neural Link socket opts in, preserving recovery after a clean bridge shutdown, while an explicit opt-out is respected.

The socket's own `close()` now sends its documented default code 1000. Its other consumer, `manager/rpc/Message.mjs`, takes the generic policy and reconnects on the next message through `sendMessage`'s closed-socket branch.

Evidence: L2 (real Chromium, native close handshakes with disposable loopback WebSocket servers) → L2 required (the client must preserve clean-close recovery). Residual: window focus/visibility returns use synthetic events on the existing listeners, as in the surrounding suite.

Change class: capability → `feat`, because the retry policy is now a reusable config even though a bug motivated it. `agent-preflight: not hosted here` (the required invocation returned Missing script); the PR baseline jobs carry the available checks in CI.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `unit/data/connection/WebSocket.spec.mjs`, “the native close callback publishes the CloseEvent fields”; the new browser arms also assert code, reason and wasClean from a real clean handshake. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the unit matrix covers normal clean default, unclean 1006, and clean going-away 1001; the local-close arm verifies code 1000 by default and preserves an explicit code/reason. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: unit opt-in arm plus `e2e/core/AiClientLateBridge.spec.mjs`, “a clean bridge close recovers through the default retry cycle and a later return”: one bounded cycle, then registration with the restarted bridge. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: companion browser opt-out arm: no retry cycle and no connection after focus/visibility returns. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: existing late-attach, backoff and error-before-close arms retained. Red-first and mutation controls below. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The opt-out deliberately ends automatic recovery after a clean normal close; the client does not fabricate an exhausted cycle to override it. Explicit socket config overrides the client default through the existing factory, and an existing supplied socket keeps its policy.

## Test Evidence

- Red-first unit run on the unmodified implementation: missing close fields and default clean-close policy fail; five controls pass.
- Remove the Socket opt-in condition: the opt-in unit arm fails (expected one retry, observed zero).
- Remove the Client's default opt-in: the clean-close recovery browser arm fails waiting for the bounded retry cycle (expected one give-up, observed zero).
- Restored implementation before the clean rebase onto `bd2a404560`: connection unit tier **10/10**, focused browser suite **5/5**. All four changed files are byte-identical after rebasing. The local browser launcher imported the canonical e2e config and changed only server binding to loopback; it was removed before commit.
- Review repair: the native-close argument arm failed on the previous signature (both omitted-code calls passed `undefined`); with `close(code = 1000, reason)`, the connection unit tier is **11/11** and the focused browser suite **5/5**. An explicit application code/reason remains unchanged. The loopback-only launcher was again removed before commit.

## Post-Merge Validation

None required beyond the committed CI-executed regression arms. No live Brain service or existing bridge was changed during validation.

**Findings:** The falsifier failed, hence RA-1. The named concern: does the socket's own clean shutdown stay closed? I ran scratch unit arms at the head (real `ws` server, not committed):

| Call | Close event | `reconnecting` | Server connections | `readyState` after 1.8 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `close()` | `{code: 1005, wasClean: true}` | 1 | 2 | OPEN |
| `close(1000)` | `{code: 1000, wasClean: true}` | 0 | 1 | CLOSED |

Destroying an open socket logs `console.error('Max reconnection attempts reached')` for either policy, on the head and on dev. Chromium 153 reports the same 1005 for `close()` and for `close(undefined, undefined)`. With `close(code = 1000, reason)`, `close()` stays closed, `destroy()` logs nothing, and the 7 `WebSocket.spec` arms pass.
